body.p: First Named Inventor Edward F. Gallagher V Attorney Docket No.: 48953-0002002 Claims (replaces all prior versions and listings):

br.br:
1. (Canceled).
2. (New) A swashplate assembly comprising:
a rotationally fixed swashplate configured to be fixed against rotating with a rotorcraft rotor; and
a plurality of pitch change links, each pitch change link configured to be coupled to a respective rotor blade of a rotorcraft and to a rotorcraft rotor to rotate with the rotor, each pitch change link configured to ride along the rotationally fixed swashplate, the rotationally fixed swashplate comprising at least one of i) a movable annular surface or ii) a plurality of interconnected and movable rail members, the annular surface or the rail members movable to form undulations or surface variations on an upper surface of the rotationally fixed swashplate and change a pitch of at least one rotor blade connected to a respective pitch change link as the respective pitch change link rides along the rotationally fixed swashplate.
3. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 2, further comprising:
a rotatable swashplate configured to reside between rotor blades of the rotor and the swashplate configured to be fixed against rotating with a rotorcraft rotor, the rotatable swashplate configured to be coupled to the rotor to rotate with the rotor, the plurality of pitch change links coupled to the rotatable swashplate; and
an annular rail coupled to the rotationally fixed swashplate to support a roller assembly of each pitch change link as each pitch change link rotates with the rotor, the roller assembly of each pitch change link arranged to engage with and ride on the annular rail such that each pitch change link is, when engaged with the annular rail, constrained to movement along the annular rail and prevented from disengaging the rail, the annular rail comprising the plurality of interconnected rail members, each member comprising a surface upon which a pitch change link rides, the annular rail comprising a plurality of actuators coupled to the rotationally fixed
First Named Inventor Edward F. Gallagher V Attorney Docket No.: 48953-0002002 swashplate and to the plurality of rail members to move at least some of the rail members independently from other rail members changing a shape of the annular rail.
4. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 3, wherein the roller assembly of each pitch change link comprises two or more rollers arranged to ride along different surfaces of the annular rail to prevent the roller assembly from disengaging the annular rail as the roller assembly of each pitch change link rides on the annular rail during rotation of the rotor blade.
5. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 2, wherein the movable rail members are interconnected by a flexible link extending through an aperture of each rail member to form a chain of interconnected rail members, wherein the flexible link comprises an adjustable fitting comprising a spring disposed between two end caps, one of the end caps threadedly connected to the flexible link to adjust, as the cap moves along the flexible link, a preload of the spring to adjust a length of the flexible link.
6. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 2, wherein each rail member comprises a tapered end and a notched end opposite the tapered end, the notched end of each rail member configured to receive a tapered end of an adjacent rail member to form, collectively, a ring- shaped rail assembly.
7. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 2, wherein each rail member comprises chamfered edges or beveled edges that allow adjacent rail members to tilt in opposite directions to allow the roller assembly to transition between tilted, adjacent rail members.
8. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 2, wherein each rail member comprises a circular angularity such that when interconnected, the rail members form together a ring-shaped annular rail.
9. (New) A swashplate assembly comprising:
First Named Inventor Edward F. Gallagher V Attorney Docket No.: 48953-0002002 a rotationally fixed swashplate configured to be fixed against rotating with a rotorcraft rotor; and
a plurality of pitch change links, each pitch change link configured to be coupled to a respective rotor blade of a rotorcraft and to a rotorcraft rotor to rotate with the rotor, each pitch change link configured to ride along the rotationally fixed swashplate, the rotationally fixed swashplate comprising at least one of i) an undulant annular surface or ii) a piezoelectric ring comprising a surface upon which a pitch change link rides, the undulant annular surface or the piezoelectric ring movable to form undulations or surface variations on an upper surface of the undulant annular surface or the piezoelectric ring and change a pitch of at least one rotor blade connected to a respective pitch change link as the respective pitch change link rides along the undulant annular surface or the piezoelectric ring.
10. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 9, further comprising:
a rotatable swashplate configured to reside between rotor blades of the rotor and the swashplate configured to be fixed against rotating with a rotorcraft rotor, the rotatable swashplate configured to be coupled to the rotor to rotate with the rotor, the plurality of pitch change links coupled to the rotatable swashplate; and
an annular track coupled to the rotationally fixed swashplate and configured to support a roller of each pitch change link riding on the annular track as each pitch change link rotates with the rotor, the annular track comprising the piezoelectric ring and a plurality of actuators arranged along the piezoelectric ring, the plurality of actuators coupled to the rotationally fixed swashplate, each actuator of the plurality of actuators configured to apply a voltage independently from the other actuators, changing a shape of the piezoelectric ring at specific azimuth locations of the piezoelectric ring and thereby changing a pitch of each rotor blade connected to a respective pitch change link as each pitch change link rides on the piezoelectric ring during rotation of the rotor blade.
11. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 10, wherein the plurality of actuators are configured to flex upwardly the piezoelectric ring at specific azimuth locations of the piezoelectric ring with respect to the rotationally fixed swashplate such that the plurality of First Named Inventor Edward F. Gallagher V Attorney Docket No.: 48953-0002002 actuators change the pitch of the rotor blade at specific azimuth locations as the roller of each pitch change link rides on the piezoelectric ring during rotation of the rotor blade.
12. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 10, wherein the plurality of actuators are configured to change a shape of the piezoelectric ring at specific azimuth locations to form an adjustable hoop with an undulating surface extending along a length of the track.
13. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 10, further comprising a processing device communicatively coupled to the plurality of actuators, the processing device configured to independently actuate each actuator based on real-time data received from rotorcraft sensors.
14. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 10, wherein the track further comprises a ring structure attached to the rotationally fixed swashplate, the ring structure defining a plurality of channels, each channel configured to receive a portion of a respective actuator from a bottom surface of the ring structure and at least a portion of the piezoelectric ring from a top surface of the ring structure to support the respective portions of the plurality of actuators and piezoelectric ring.
15. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 10, wherein the plurality of actuators comprise voltage generators and the piezoelectric ring comprises a plurality of piezoelectric members that collectively form the piezoelectric ring, each actuator of the plurality of actuators configured to apply a voltage independently from the other actuators to change a shape of at least some of the plurality of piezoelectric members independently from other piezoelectric members.
16. (New) A swashplate assembly comprising:
a rotationally fixed swashplate configured to be fixed against rotating with a rotorcraft rotor; and
a plurality of pitch change links, each pitch change link configured to be coupled to a respective rotor blade of a rotorcraft and to a rotorcraft rotor to rotate with the rotor, each pitch change link configured to ride on a track of the rotationally fixed swashplate, the track
First Named Inventor Edward F. Gallagher V Attorney Docket No.: 48953-0002002 comprising at least one of i) a plurality of movable surfaces or ii) a plurality of changeable magnetic fields to change an upper surface or an annular magnetic field of the track and change a pitch of each rotor blade connected to a respective pitch change link as each pitch change link rides on the movable surfaces or the magnetic fields during rotation of the rotor blade.
17. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 16, further comprising:
a rotatable swashplate configured to reside between rotor blades of the rotor and the swashplate fixed against rotating with a rotorcraft rotor, the rotatable swashplate configured to be coupled to the rotor to rotate with the rotor, the plurality of pitch change links coupled to the rotatable swashplate; and
wherein the magnetic fields comprise electromagnetic fields and the track comprises a plurality of electromagnets arranged along and coupled to the rotationally fixed swashplate, each of the plurality of electromagnets configured to generate a field of the electromagnetic fields to repel a magnet of each pitch change link as each pitch change link rotates with the rotor, the magnet oriented to produce a magnetic field in a direction opposite to the electromagnetic fields of the plurality of electromagnets, each of the plurality of electromagnets configured to generate an electromagnetic field with a strength independent from the electromagnetic fields generated by the other electromagnets to change a pitch of each rotor blade connected to a respective pitch change link as the magnet of each pitch change link is repelled from the plurality of electromagnets during rotation of the rotor blade.
18. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 17, further comprising a processing device electrically coupled to the plurality of electromagnets, each of the electromagnets comprising a conductor around a magnetic core and electrically coupled to the processing device, the processing device configured to change one or more parameters of a current flowing through the conductor around the magnetic core to change a strength of the respective electromagnetic field.
19. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 18, wherein the processing device is configured to change the strength of the respective electromagnetic field based on real-time data received, by the processing device, from rotorcraft sensors.
First Named Inventor Edward F. Gallagher V Attorney Docket No.: 48953-0002002
20. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 17, wherein the magnet of each pitch change link is a second electromagnet, each of the plurality of electromagnets configured to generate an electromagnetic field to repel the second electromagnet of each pitch change link as each pitch change link rotates with the rotor, each second electromagnet configured to generate a second electromagnetic field in a direction opposite to the electromagnetic fields of the plurality of electromagnets.
21. (New) The swashplate assembly of claim 17, wherein the plurality of electromagnets are configured to change a strength of their respective electromagnetic field to change the pitch of the rotor blade at specific azimuth locations as the magnet of each pitch change link is repelled by the plurality of electromagnetic fields during rotation of the rotor blade.
